From 785c9f411eb2d9a6076d3511c631587d5e676bf3 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Krzysztof Kozlowski <krzk@kernel.org>
Date: Thu, 21 Feb 2019 12:45:52 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] clk: samsung: exynos5: Fix kfree() of const memory on setting
 driver_override

Platform driver driver_override field should not be initialized from
const memory because the core later kfree() it.  If driver_override is
manually set later through sysfs, kfree() of old value leads to:

    $ echo "new_value" > /sys/bus/platform/drivers/.../driver_override

    kernel BUG at ../mm/slub.c:3960!
    Internal error: Oops - BUG: 0 [#1] PREEMPT SMP ARM
    ...
    (kfree) from [<c058e8c0>] (platform_set_driver_override+0x84/0xac)
    (platform_set_driver_override) from [<c058e908>] (driver_override_store+0x20/0x34)
    (driver_override_store) from [<c031f778>] (kernfs_fop_write+0x100/0x1dc)
    (kernfs_fop_write) from [<c0296de8>] (__vfs_write+0x2c/0x17c)
    (__vfs_write) from [<c02970c4>] (vfs_write+0xa4/0x188)
    (vfs_write) from [<c02972e8>] (ksys_write+0x4c/0xac)
    (ksys_write) from [<c0101000>] (ret_fast_syscall+0x0/0x28)

The clk-exynos5-subcmu driver uses override only for the purpose of
creating meaningful names for children devices (matching names of power
domains, e.g. DISP, MFC).  The driver_override was not developed for
this purpose so just switch to default names of devices to fix the
issue.

Fixes: b06a532bf1fa ("clk: samsung: Add Exynos5 sub-CMU clock driver")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Krzysztof Kozlowski <krzk@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Geert Uytterhoeven <geert+renesas@glider.be>
Signed-off-by: Stephen Boyd <sboyd@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/clk/samsung/clk-exynos5-subcmu.c b/drivers/clk/samsung/clk-exynos5-subcmu.c
index d07ef26bd052..8ae44b5db4c2 100644
--- a/drivers/clk/samsung/clk-exynos5-subcmu.c
+++ b/drivers/clk/samsung/clk-exynos5-subcmu.c
@@ -138,12 +138,11 @@ static int __init exynos5_clk_register_subcmu(struct device *parent,
 	struct platform_device *pdev;
 	int ret;
 
-	pdev = platform_device_alloc(info->pd_name, -1);
+	pdev = platform_device_alloc("exynos5-subcmu", PLATFORM_DEVID_AUTO);
 	if (!pdev)
 		return -ENOMEM;
 
 	pdev->dev.parent = parent;
-	pdev->driver_override = "exynos5-subcmu";
 	platform_set_drvdata(pdev, (void *)info);
 	of_genpd_add_device(&genpdspec, &pdev->dev);
 	ret = platform_device_add(pdev);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/clk/samsung/clk-exynos5-subcmu.c`**
   - The line that initializes `pdev->driver_override` with a constant string `"exynos5-subcmu"` has been removed.
   - The `platform_device_alloc` function call has been modified to use a hardcoded string `"exynos5-subcmu"` instead of `info->pd_name`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in the `clk-exynos5-subcmu.c` file addresses a bug related to the improper handling of the `driver_override` field. By removing the initialization of `driver_override` from constant memory, the patch prevents a potential kernel crash that occurs when the system attempts to free this memory later. The change ensures that the driver uses default naming for devices instead of relying on the `driver_override`, which was not intended for this purpose. This adjustment resolves the issue while maintaining the functionality of the driver.

    ...
    (kfree) from [<c058e8c0>] (platform_set_driver_override+0x84/0xac)

    (ksys_write) from [<c0101000>] (ret_fast_syscall+0x0/0x28)

Fixes: b06a532bf1fa ("clk: samsung: Add Exynos5 sub-CMU clock driver")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Krzysztof Kozlowski <krzk@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Geert Uytterhoeven <geert+renesas@glider.be>
Signed-off-by: Stephen Boyd <sboyd@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug is caused by initializing the `driver_override` field of the platform device with a constant string. This leads to a situation where the memory allocated for `driver_override` is later freed by the kernel, resulting in a kernel crash when the value is manually changed through sysfs, as the original constant memory cannot be safely freed.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int __init exynos5_clk_register_subcmu(struct device *parent,
 					 const struct exynos5_subcmu_info *info,
 					      struct device_node *pd_node)
 {
 	struct of_phandle_args genpdspec = { .np = pd_node };
 	struct platform_device *pdev;
 	int ret;
 
-	pdev = platform_device_alloc(info->pd_name, -1);
+	pdev = platform_device_alloc("exynos5-subcmu", PLATFORM_DEVID_AUTO);
 	if (!pdev)
 		return -ENOMEM;
 
 	pdev->dev.parent = parent;
-	pdev->driver_override = "exynos5-subcmu";
 	platform_set_drvdata(pdev, (void *)info);
 	of_genpd_add_device(&genpdspec, &pdev->dev);
 	ret = platform_device_add(pdev);
 	if (ret)
 		platform_device_put(pdev);
 
 	return ret;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
pdev->driver_override = "exynos5-subcmu";
```
Reason:
This statement initializes the `driver_override` field of the platform device with a constant string. Since this memory is constant, it cannot be safely freed later when the kernel attempts to free the `driver_override` value, leading to a kernel crash when the value is changed through sysfs.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
pdev = platform_device_alloc("exynos5-subcmu", PLATFORM_DEVID_AUTO);
```
Reason:
This change allocates the platform device with a proper name instead of using a constant string for `driver_override`. By not setting `driver_override` to a constant string, the issue of attempting to free constant memory is avoided, thus preventing the kernel crash.
